title: Turner 2022 antidepressant update: transparency can improve without eliminating reporting bias
summary: A longitudinal status-history record for reporting bias: newer antidepressant trials showed improved transparent reporting compared with older trials, especially among negative trials, but outcome-dependent reporting persisted.

status_history.note: Promoted in rev0009 as a reporting-bias / file-drawer audit record.

place.scope: 4 newer antidepressants / 30 FDA-registered phase II/III acute monotherapy trials

claims.claim: Turner et al. 2022 repeated the FDA-versus-journal logic for 30 newer antidepressant trials and found reporting bias persisted but appeared diminished compared with the older cohort.
what_would_change_status: A later reanalysis or correction changes the newer-cohort trial set or transparent-publication classification.

claims.claim: Within the newer cohort, transparent publication occurred for all 15 FDA-positive trials and for 7 of 15 FDA-negative trials; six negative trials were unpublished and two were treated as not transparently published as positive/pooled reports.
